newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania cen.bank sees $1.0 bln fx reserves end-96.
newsitem.headline: Romania cen.bank sees $1.0 bln fx reserves end-96.

text.p: Romania's central bank (BNR) governor was quoted as saying on Tuesday that the BNR hoped to end 1996 with foreign exchange reserves of $1.0 billion, the highest level since the fall of communism in 1989.
The BNR was also planning to double or even triple its reserves in the years ahead to boost Romania's credibility.

"We hope to end the year with reserves of roughly $1.0 billion, after fully paying the external debt service for 1996, which stands at $1.2 billion," Mugur Isarescu told the daily newspaper Romania Libera.

According to lastest official data, foreign exchange reserves rose to $1.0 billion in October from $703.6 million in September as the central bank had almost ended a 1996 borrowing programme from international markets.

Over the past two months, the BNR raised some $270 million in five-year Samurai bonds and $175 million from a syndicated loan. The bank was entitled to draw $1.5 billion from private capital markets this year and has so far raised $1.4 billion.
"Total BNR reserves -- including hard currency and gold -- amount to more than $2.0 billion, which is high compared with previous years," Isarescu said.
The bank's gold reserves stand at 87 tonnes, or $1.1 billion at market prices.
"Starting 1997, we must begin the battle to double and even triple the reserves...which is essential for international credibility," Isarescu said.

He said a credible foreign exchange reserve should cover four to six months of imports. "At the current level of our foreign trade it means $3.0 billion to $4.0 billion," he said. -- Luli Popescu, Bucharest newsroom, 40-1 3120264
